featured_reviews.name: Prashant Tawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently donated blood at this blood bank and was informed that my blood had tested positive for hepatitis C antibodies using the ELISA Generation 4 method. Naturally, this news was extremely concerning, so I took it upon myself to get retested at a private lab. The private lab conducted two tests—one using the rapid method and the other using the ELFA method. Both of these tests came back negative for hepatitis C antibodies. To be absolutely sure, I also did an HCV RNA PCR test, which is the most reliable test for detecting an active hepatitis C infection. Thankfully, the result was "NOT DETECTED," meaning there was no active virus in my blood.

This whole experience has caused me unnecessary stress and confusion. I fully understand that antibody tests can sometimes give false positives, but I believe the blood bank should be more cautious and thorough before alarming donors with such serious results. Furthermore, after receiving the initial notification, I reached out to the blood bank multiple times seeking guidance on what to do next, but they have stopped responding to my queries. They haven’t provided any further support, leaving me in the dark about whether I can donate blood in the future or what steps I should take.

This lack of communication and support from the blood bank is extremely disappointing, especially when dealing with such sensitive health concerns. I advise others to be cautious and double-check their results if they receive any alarming notifications from this blood bank. I hope the blood bank improves their processes, both in terms of accuracy and in providing proper guidance to donors.

I had a very disappointing experience at Neptune Diagnostic and Fetal Medicine.
When I visited for a sonography at around 11:00 AM, the staff initially informed me that the total cost would be ₹5000. After that, I confirmed with my doctor and went back for the sonography after about half an hour. At that time, the staff suddenly told me that the total cost would be ₹6500. After returning in the evening, I was again made to wait for around 2 more hours. There seemed to be no respect for patients’ time.
For such a large organization, the time management and coordination are very poor. There was no senior person available, and the staff seemed to be working only based on guidance from each other, which created confusion.
Overall, I had a very bad service experience. *The doctor is very good and very cooperative* but the management and service system are very poor. Because of this experience, I will never visit this place again and will not recommend it to anyone.

I have the recording of the conversation about the charges and staff communication. If needed, I can provide it as proof. I will also share my experience on other review platforms so that other patients can be aware of the service quality.

HbA1c Test: Purpose, Procedure, Normal Range & Results
May 26, 2026 - By Lupin Diagnostics
India has over 10.1 crore people living with diabetes. A daily finger-prick reading captures just one moment. The HbA1c test normal range tells a fuller story. This simple blood test reveals your average blood sugar over three months. Here is everything you need to know about it.
What Is the HbA1c Test and How Does It Work?
Glucose in your blood naturally sticks to haemoglobin, the protein inside red blood cells. The more sugar in your blood, the more gets attached. Since red blood cells live for roughly three months, the HbA1c test captures your average blood sugar level over that entire period.
This makes it far more reliable than a single fasting reading. A fasting test changes with your last meal or stress levels. Glycated haemoglobin, on the other hand, reflects steady patterns. Think of it as a three-month report card for your blood sugar.
Here is how it differs from routine glucose checks:
A fasting blood sugar test measures glucose at one point in time.
The HbA1c test shows a percentage reflecting 90-day glucose control.
It does not swing based on a recent meal or exercise session.

In healthy blood, this happens slowly. When inflammation is present, the cells tend to clump together and sink more quickly than usual. ESR is a simple, widely used marker for inflammation. Your liver handles a lot: filtering toxins, making proteins, and producing digestive enzymes. Since your liver works silently, most damage often goes unnoticed until it becomes serious. An LFT is a group of blood tests that check how well the liver is performing.

The test typically measures ALT (SGPT), AST (SGOT), bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, and albumin levels. Together, these markers reveal the type and location of liver damage. Unlike a single blood sugar reading, an LFT panel paints a broader picture of your liver's overall health.

Early detection matters! The WHO states that 254 million people were diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B in 2022, with an increase of 1.2 million every year. In 2022 alone, the infection caused roughly 1.1 million deaths, mostly from cirrhosis and liver cancer.
